workflow_pattern: This is a 'V2_4cand_compare_fork_multiple' style workflow. It requires the following operations, in roughly this order: select repo by comparison metric, fork repository preserving name, append multiple reference links readme. The task should combine these operations into one coherent, realistic request without listing them as separate steps.
question: Hey! I've been comparing static-site tooling for a big documentation-site migration and narrowed it down to 4 candidates: gohugoio's hugo, getzola's zola, jekyll's jekyll, and vercel's next.js. First, narrow the list down to only the candidates that have more than 10,000 stars. Then, among the repositories that survive that filter, fork whichever one has the fewest open issues — that popularity-plus-low-friction combination is exactly what I'm looking for in a tool we'll depend on long-term. Keep the same name as the original repo. Then add three reference links at the bottom of the README.md file pointing to the other three repos like this: '1. related project [repo name 1](the link of repo 1)', '2. related project [repo name 2](the link of repo 2)', '3. related project [repo name 3](the link of repo 3)'. This kind of cross-referencing will help future maintainers see how these projects relate to each other.
